html:
Vlad III, prince of Wallachia, in what is now southern Romania, who ruled three times between 1448 and 1476 and fought the Ottoman Empire. He is known as the Impaler for killing enemies on stakes, and as Dracula, "son of the Dragon", after his father Vlad II Dracul.

As a boy he was held hostage at the Ottoman court with his brother Radu. Wallachia's princes were made and unmade by Hungary and the Ottomans.

In his main reign, from 1456 to 1462, he crushed the boyars and impaled thousands of enemies, criminals and Turkish prisoners. He stopped paying tribute to Mehmed II, who had just taken Constantinople, and in 1462 led a night attack on the sultan's camp. When Mehmed reached Vlad's capital he found a forest of impaled bodies. Vlad was driven out and held for years by the Hungarian king, then regained his throne in 1476 and was killed within months.

German pamphlets made him a monster; Romanians also remember him as a defender of the country. Bram Stoker borrowed his name for the novel Dracula in 1897.
